issues.display_title: Issue #1784: Add optional Stripe Test Clock support to V2 subscriptions
issues.main_description_html:
Goal

Add optional Stripe Test Clock support to the V2 subscription creation flow.

Requirements

  • Accept test_clock on POST /v2/payment/subscription/subs.
  • Default to false to preserve current behavior.
  • Accept only true or false values.
  • Allow test_clock=true only for Stripe test-mode users.
  • Create a new Test Clock and attach it to the Stripe Customer.
  • Leave the legacy app/Class/Payment/SubscriptionClass.php flow unchanged.

Verification

  • Focused Test Clock tests pass.
  • Existing space-addon transaction-ID test passes.
  • PR: #1783

Result

  • Implemented optional test_clock support in the V2 Stripe subscription flow.
  • Added strict parsing for true/false, with validation errors for invalid values.
  • Restricted test_clock=true to Stripe test mode.
  • When enabled, creates a Stripe Test Clock using the current Unix time and attaches it to the new Stripe Customer before subscription creation.
  • Preserved the default behavior when test_clock is omitted or false.
  • Kept the legacy subscription flow unchanged.
  • Added focused coverage for clock creation, customer attachment, disabled behavior, timestamp usage, and query-value parsing.
  • Implemented in commit eae488ad8 and delivered through PR #1783.

issues.display_title: Issue #1780: Fix test-reset-subscription to cancel Stripe test subscriptions safely
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

POST /test-reset-subscription resets local DB subscription fields but does not cancel Stripe subscriptions whose IDs start with sub_.

Current behavior:

  • Authenticates user by Authorization token.
  • Sets users.space_addon = 0, users.space_addon_plan = null, users.subscribtion = 0.
  • If user_extra_data.recurring_profile starts with I-, cancels PayPal subscription.
  • Clears user_extra_data.recurring_profile, current_recurring_plan, check_space.
  • Deletes unsubscribes rows.
  • Does not cancel Stripe subscription IDs in recurring_profile.

This can leave active Stripe test subscriptions detached from GoThru accounts.

Fix

  • Match /test-reset-photo-studio-subscription behavior and block non-test users with HelperClass::isUseStripeTestMode().
  • If recurring_profile starts with sub_, cancel it through Stripe test client before clearing DB fields.
  • Keep PayPal I- cancellation behavior.
  • Return proper status codes using HelperClass::getStatusCode(), not always 409.

Acceptance

  • Test user with recurring_profile=sub_* gets Stripe test subscription canceled, then DB fields cleared.
  • Test user with recurring_profile=I-* still cancels PayPal subscription.
  • Non-test user gets 403 and no DB mutation.
  • Existing local reset behavior remains unchanged after successful cancellation.

Result

Implemented by the developer:

  • Restricted /test-reset-subscription to Stripe test-mode users; non-test users receive HTTP 403 without database mutation.
  • Added cancellation of Stripe subscriptions with sub_ IDs through the Stripe test client before clearing local subscription data.
  • Preserved PayPal cancellation for I- recurring profiles.
  • Moved local database reset after provider cancellation to avoid clearing state when cancellation fails.
  • Updated error responses to use HelperClass::getStatusCode() instead of always returning HTTP 409.

Developer commit: 62c2735d (fix: cancel stripe subscriptions on test reset).

issues.display_title: Issue #1778: Generate invoice + send email in record-stripe-recurring-transactions cron
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Wire invoice PDF generation and the "Notify New Invoice" Plunk email into GET /cronjob/record-stripe-recurring-transactions, so recurring Stripe renewal charges get the same invoice+email treatment as real-time checkout/upgrade/downgrade flows.

Current state

RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper::processCharge() (app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper.php:93-128) only logs the charge to cc_logs_stripe and inserts a deduped cc_purchase row via insertPurchase() (:198-214). No invoice PDF gets generated and no email gets sent for this path — confirmed no call to InvoiceHelper or EmailClass anywhere in this file or CronjobController::recordStripeRecurringTransactions() (app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/CronjobController.php:293-304).

By contrast, the real-time subscription flow already does both: InvoiceHelper::prepareInvoiceData() (app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Invoice/InvoiceHelper.php:71-110) generates the PDF, and SubscriptionClass::sendSubscriptionSuccessEmail() (app/Class/Payment/SubscriptionClass.php:421) sends via EmailClass->send().

The EmailTemplateUID::NOTIFY_NEW_INVOICE constant (823bd4de-26b5-418e-8ed1-21433affe0f3) now exists (added in #1777) but nothing calls it yet.

Target state

After insertPurchase() succeeds for a charge in processCharge():

  1. Call InvoiceHelper::prepareInvoiceData($userId, $charge->id, $datePurchase) to generate/locate the invoice PDF (mirrors SubscriptionHelpers::generateAndSaveInvoice() at app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Subscription/SubscriptionHelpers.php:459-494).
  2. Resolve the user's email + name (billing address or UsersClass user info — match whichever SubscriptionClass/InvoiceHelper already uses for consistency).
  3. Send the invoice notification via EmailClass->send($email, EmailTemplateUID::NOTIFY_NEW_INVOICE, ['customer_name' => ...]), gated by the send_email flag (see below) — PDF still generates either way, only the email send is skippable.
  4. Add a notified/emailed counter to $counters in RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper so run()'s response reflects how many invoice emails actually sent.
  5. Wrap invoice+email in the existing per-charge try/catch (run():41-51) so one failed invoice/email doesn't abort the batch — log and continue, same pattern as the existing charge-processing error handling.

Opt-out flag: email sends by default. Add ?send_email=0 to disable it for that run (e.g. re-running the cron to backfill cc_purchase/PDFs without re-notifying users). Mirror the existing test_mode pattern:

  • CronjobController::recordStripeRecurringTransactions() (:293-304): $isSendEmail = $request->boolean('send_email', true);, pass into RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper (constructor arg or run() param).
  • RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper::run(): thread the flag down to the invoice/email step in processCharge(); PDF generation (step 1) always runs regardless of the flag, only step 3 (the actual EmailClass->send() call) is gated.

Scope

  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper.php: __construct(), run(), processCharge(), insertPurchase() (or a new private method called right after it), $counters.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/CronjobController.php: recordStripeRecurringTransactions() — read send_email query param, pass through.
  • Constructor: inject InvoiceHelper and EmailClass (same pattern as existing CCLogClass/CCTransClass injection at :28-34).

Out of scope

  • Changing the Plunk template content itself (already set up in #1777).
  • Retrofitting invoice+email onto any other cron (checkExpireSubscription, processUnsubscribesPhotoStudioTable, etc.).
  • Deduping emails across multiple cron runs beyond what isDuplicateTransaction() already guarantees at the cc_purchase level.

Risk / test plan

  • Run ?test_mode=1 against a Stripe test account with a known recurring charge, confirm a PDF lands in /data/moderation/{user_id}/receipt/ and the customer receives the Plunk email.
  • Force a charge with user_id=0 (unresolvable subscription) and confirm it's still skipped before invoice/email (no PDF/email generated for unmatched users, per existing skipped_no_user counter).
  • Re-run the cron over the same date range and confirm no duplicate email sends (guarded by isDuplicateTransaction()).
  • One bad invoice/email must not stop the rest of the batch — verify via the try/catch counter.
  • Call with ?send_email=0: confirm PDF still generates but no email sends, and the notified counter stays 0.
  • Call with no send_email param: confirm it still defaults to sending (matches current always-on legacy behavior).
